body.x: Think-Soft (CEO JooHyun Park) announced its participation in CES 2025, which will be held from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas, USA, at the K-Startup Pavilion.

Think-Soft is a South Korean company specializing in automation control systems for semiconductor and display manufacturing processes. The company also develops IoT-based particle sensors and monitoring systems, offering tailored solutions to clients. Through these innovations, Think-Soft aims to establish smart factory solutions that drive industry growth.

At CES 2025, Think-Soft will showcase its advanced automation technologies, including CIM and SECS/GEM equipment control systems, AI-powered logistics management system LIMS, and IoT particle sensor-based cleanroom monitoring solutions. The company plans to highlight its expertise in automation technology and its ability to support productivity improvements in high-tech manufacturing.

A key feature of Think-Soft’s offerings is its conveyor shaft grounding and particle monitoring system, which was developed in collaboration with NOVO. This system detects grounding conditions in real-time within a range of 0.0–246.9Ω, helping prevent static electricity risks, a critical issue in semiconductor and display manufacturing.

Think-Soft is actively pursuing expansion into the Chinese market, leveraging its expertise to address the vast demand in the region’s semiconductor and display industries. The company aims to capitalize on the booming investment in smart manufacturing and automation solutions in China.

A Think-Soft representative explained, “Our participation in CES 2025 will showcase the capabilities of our in-house R&D and collaboration networks. We will offer various process automation solutions to potential clients and industry stakeholders. The event will also provide a platform to connect with global industry leaders and identify partners to support our entry into international markets.”

The representative added, “China’s semiconductor and display industries are at the forefront of our expansion plans. We are committed to investing significantly and strengthening distribution channels to establish a presence in this key market. By collaborating with local companies, we aim to expand our influence into advanced manufacturing sites worldwide.”

AVING News, which has covered CES for 19 consecutive years, continues to bridge the gap for Korean SMEs and startups looking to expand globally. To promote Korean startups worldwide, AVING will host its Broadcasting Zone at the Venetian Expo, featuring the CES Media Day Startup Conference and global media interviews. AVING’s international media partners will cover these programs.
Following CES 2025, AVING will co-host review conferences with participating companies in Korea, offering a platform for increased visibility and improved corporate image.
